title: SaaS / Supply & Services Agreement Review (Singapore & Common Law)
practice: Review of SaaS, cloud, managed services, technology supply and services agreements under Singapore law, covering SLAs, IP and licensing, data protection, liability, indemnities, and termination.

columns_config.name: Agreement Structure
columns_config.prompt: Describe the contract structure: master services agreement, order forms/statements of work, SLA schedules, DPA, acceptable use policy, support policy. Identify which documents are incorporated by reference and which version governs. State whether the contract is a true subscription (right of use) or involves delivery of bespoke development (matters for IP ownership). Identify each party and its role (provider, customer, reseller, subcontractor).

columns_config.name: Scope of Services & Deliverables
columns_config.prompt: Summarise what is being supplied: software-as-a-service access, hosting, professional services, support tiers, training, or a combination. Identify dependencies on customer obligations (data provision, third-party licences, network access) and any acceptance testing regime for deliverables. Flag scope gaps or dependencies that would let the provider avoid performance.

columns_config.name: SLA / Service Levels
columns_config.prompt: Extract the SLA terms: uptime commitment (e.g. 99.9%), measurement window and excluded time (maintenance windows, force majeure, customer-caused failures), remedy mechanism (service credits, refund, right to terminate for chronic failure), credit caps, and whether credits are the sole remedy. Assess whether the SLA is enforceable in practice (are reports generated and audited?) and whether chronic-failure termination thresholds (e.g. X months below target in Y rolling months) exist. Flag if there is NO SLA at all and the customer is left to general contract law only.

columns_config.name: Fees, Payment & Price Variation
columns_config.prompt: State fees, payment terms, currency, GST treatment (Singapore GST under the GST Act 1993 - note whether the supplier is GST-registered and whether prices are GST-inclusive; also GST on digital services for overseas suppliers), late-payment interest, price-escalation rights at renewal (cap? notice period?), and taxes/withholdings for cross-border payment. Flag any unilateral price-increase right without a matching termination-on-notice right.

columns_config.name: IP Ownership & Licence Scope
columns_config.prompt: Analyse the IP provisions: (a) ownership of Background IP (usually supplier) and Foreground IP / custom developments (who owns? is it assignment or mere licence?); (b) scope of the licence granted (exclusive/non-exclusive, transferable, sub-licensable, perpetual, royalty-free, limited to internal business use); (c) what happens to customer data on exit (export rights, format, timeline); (d) supplier's use of aggregated/anonymised or derived data - a common erosion of customer rights; and (e) whether customer feedback or improvement rights let the supplier reuse customer IP. Reference the Copyright Act 2021 (SG) for assignment formalities (s 130: assignments must be in writing and signed).

columns_config.name: Third-Party & Open-Source IP
columns_config.prompt: Identify third-party components, open-source libraries (copyleft vs permissive licences), and third-party data/content used in the service. Assess IP indemnity coverage for open-source contamination claims and whether the indemnity excludes claims arising from customer modification or combination. Note any obligation on the supplier to disclose the open-source stack.

columns_config.name: Data Protection / PDPA
columns_config.prompt: Assess the data-protection provisions against the Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (SG): (a) is there a DPA and does the supplier act as a 'data intermediary' (PDPA s 4(2)) processing personal data on behalf of the customer, triggering s 5A (protection) and Part 3A obligations; (b) does the DPA impose the full set of PDPA obligations on the supplier including security, retention limitation (s 25), notification of data breach to the customer (data intermediaries are separately obliged to notify the organisation on whose behalf they process data - see PDPA Part 3A (s 5A) and the 2021 data breach notification subsidiary legislation; verify the operative provisions), and deletion/return on exit; (c) cross-border transfer restrictions (PDPA Part 6A, including transfer-limitation obligations and reliance on the prescribed Certification standard or contractual Binding Corporate Rules); and (d) who is controller vs intermediary if the supplier uses sub-processors or AI/ML training on customer data. Flag training-on-customer-data clauses expressly.

columns_config.name: Cybersecurity & Security Practices
columns_config.prompt: Summarise the security representations: standards claimed (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, CSA STAR, MTCS SS 584), breach notification timelines (and whether they align with PDPA's 3-day notification obligation to the PDPC once a breach is assessed as notifiable, per s 26D and the Regulations), penetration testing rights, audit rights and their limits, and incident response commitments. Flag any clause that makes the customer responsible for security of a hosted environment.

columns_config.name: Liability Cap & Exclusions
columns_config.prompt: Extract the liability regime: (a) the cap (fixed amount, multiple of fees paid in the trailing 12 months, or uncapped); (b) what is EXCLUDED from the cap (usually direct loss only, and often carve-outs for breach of confidentiality, IP indemnity, death/personal injury, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, and regulatory fines); (c) exclusion of indirect, special, consequential loss and 'loss of profits, revenue, goodwill, anticipated savings, or data' - and whether loss of data is carved back in; (d) any reference to the Singapore common-law position (unfair contract terms doctrine under the Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977 (SG) - s 3 and Schedule 2 reasonableness test for exclusion clauses in B2B contracts where one party deals as a consumer or on written standard terms of business). Assess whether the cap is realistic against the maximum exposure under the contract.

columns_config.name: Indemnities
columns_config.prompt: List each indemnity (IP infringement, breach of data-protection obligations, employee claims, regulatory fines, gross negligence) and for each state: who indemnifies whom, whether it is uncapped or inside the general cap, whether it excludes consequential loss, and whether there is a conduct/settlement-approval procedure. Note that under SG common law indemnities and damages caps are construed strictly, and that an indemnity for regulatory fines may be void or limited as a matter of public policy in some jurisdictions.

columns_config.name: Warranties & Disclaimers
columns_config.prompt: State the express warranties (compliance with law, non-infringement, workmanlike services, malware-free, conformity to documentation) and any disclaimers (no warranty of uninterrupted or error-free service, 'as is'). Check consistency with the implied warranties under the Sale of Goods Act 1979 (SG) and the Supply of Services provisions of the Sale of Goods and Services Act, and whether a B2B agreement can exclude or modify them (note the Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977 reasonableness test again). Flag if the supplier disclaims all warranties to a degree that guts the deal for the customer.

columns_config.name: Term, Renewal & Termination
columns_config.prompt: State the initial term, auto-renewal mechanics and notice period, and every termination right: for breach (cure period?), for insolvency (and whether the SG insolvency moratorium under the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution Act 2018 - including s 64 of the IRDA restraining contractual termination - is addressed), for convenience (any break fee?), for chronic SLA failure, and for change of control. Note what happens on termination: transition assistance, data export, payment of accrued fees, survival clauses (which clauses survive and for how long).

columns_config.name: Insurance & Subcontracting
columns_config.prompt: Identify insurance obligations (types, limits, evidence, and whether certificates are required annually) and subcontracting rules (consent required? flow-down of confidentiality, security and data-protection obligations? supplier liability for subcontractor breaches?).

columns_config.name: Force Majeure & Hardship
columns_config.prompt: Summarise the force majeure clause: the events listed (is cyberattack, pandemic, or government action included?), notice requirements, duration threshold for termination, and whether payment obligations are suspended. Note that SG common law does not imply force majeure (it must be contractual) and that frustration under the Contract (Rights of Third Parties) provisions or the common law is narrow - flag if the clause is missing or very narrow.

columns_config.name: Governing Law, Disputes & Third-Party Rights
columns_config.prompt: State governing law, forum (Singapore courts / SIAC / ICC arbitration), escalation ladder (executive negotiation, mediation before litigation, SIMC where applicable), injunctive relief carve-out, and the operation of the Contract (Rights of Third Parties) Act 2001 (SG) - does the contract exclude or include third-party beneficiaries (e.g. affiliates, end users)? Flag any arbitration clause that would exclude the ability to get urgent injunctive relief in court (usually carved out; check).

columns_config.name: Key Risks & Redlines
columns_config.prompt: List the top 5-7 risks in this contract for the party we are advising (identify which side we are on), each with: the specific clause, why it is a risk, and a concrete redline or fallback. Cover at least: liability cap adequacy, data-protection gap, IP ownership gap, SLA enforceability, auto-renewal trap, and any unilateral amendment right (esp. for the supplier to amend policies or pricing mid-term).

columns_config.name: Overall Assessment
columns_config.prompt: Overall assessment of this agreement as drafted for our client's position:
